description: Enforces strict adherence to the mandatory procedural and substantive requirements of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) notifications, prohibiting post-facto regularizations and ensuring robust expert appraisal and public consultation.
application_scenario: Use when evaluating the validity of an Environmental Clearance (EC) where the project proponent allegedly concealed material facts, bypassed public consultation, or where the regulatory authority granted post-facto approval or failed to conduct a reasoned expert appraisal.
reasoning_flow: Identify the proposed project and determine its categorization under the governing statutory Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) framework requiring prior clearance.
Examine whether the project proponent made a full, transparent, and candid disclosure of all ecological baseline data (e.g., in Form 1) without suppressing material facts.
Assess whether the mandatory stages of the EIA process, including meaningful public consultation and critical evaluation of public objections, were strictly adhered to.

Scrutinize the decision of the expert appraisal body (EAC/SEIAA) to verify if it independently applied its mind, recorded substantive reasons, and evaluated the environmental consequences rather than acting mechanically or cryptically.

Invalidate the clearance, or strike down regularization attempts (such as ex-post-facto approvals), if there is a substantive breach of the EIA procedures, invoking the precautionary principle to prevent irreversible ecological harm.
example_application: A project proponent applies for an EC for a new airport but fails to disclose the presence of thousands of trees and eco-sensitive zones in the application form. The expert committee recommends clearance without analyzing public objections. The court suspends the EC, holding that material concealment and the expert body's abdication of its appraisal duties vitiate the clearance process.
shared_pattern: All three cases hinge on the indispensable requirement to strictly follow the statutory sequence and substantive mandates of the EIA Notifications (prior clearance, genuine public hearing, and reasoned expert appraisal), rejecting administrative shortcuts, material concealments, or post-facto regularizations.
scope_exclusions: Do not use for general tortious environmental pollution claims (like nuisance or negligence) or routine pollution control board consent renewals that do not involve the statutory EIA/EC approval process.
